items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and moving-average stack, then track the change in the VIX band versus the prior window, and overlay the intraday session type and VWAP plus the option-flow premium lean and single most-unusual print, to judge whether an index near its high is being confirmed by broad participation or is compressing — thin breadth with falling volatility — before it resolves.
items.note: Price is near the high but participation underneath it remains thin while volatility has quietly compressed, a combination worth watching pre-market. SPY last printed 762.6, about 1.96% under its 52-week high, in a bull-stacked moving-average regime (50-day distance +1.58%, 200-day +8.24%, 126-day momentum +12.01%) — yet only 29.99% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day, a 30.01-point shortfall below the 60% broad-participation line, so leadership is narrow rather than broad. What is genuinely new this window is that the VIX has eased to 15.7 from the prior 16.01 band even as breadth stays pinned near 30%: falling headline volatility alongside thin participation is a compression, not a broad all-clear. Underneath, the prior session was a trend-day-down auction with VWAP 764.84 above spot, and option premium is put-heavy across 12 tickers with 1942 contracts clearing the $250k bar inside 30 days, the single most-unusual print an AVGO 420 put at $46.2M on 12.3x its open interest. So a calm-looking tape is carrying a narrow, hedged market. Watch whether breadth recovers back above the 60% line to confirm the calm, or a daily close below 760.00 resolves the narrow-breadth top downward while volatility is still cheap.
items.title: SPY holds about 2% under its 52-week high while daily breadth stays narrow at 29.99% of constituents positive — a 30-point shortfall under the 60% line — even as VIX eases to 15.7

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative dealer gamma; flip=765.51; callWall=770; putWall=765; expectedMove=8.21; spot=762.6
items.method: Read the options-structure gamma sign with its flip and wall levels against current benchmark spot and compare the wall-versus-spot geometry to the prior window, size the expected-move band around spot, confirm the dealer scenario and conviction from the gamma playbook, then overlay the intraday session type and VWAP and the VIX band, to judge whether losing the near wall in negative gamma is positioning dealers to extend a break or whether the next shelf holds.
items.note: The genuinely new structural feature this window is that spot no longer sits between the dealer walls — it has dropped beneath the lower one. Signed dealer gamma is negative, and SPY near 762.6 is below the 765.51 flip AND below the 765 put wall, with the 770 call wall well overhead; the front expected move is plus or minus 8.21, a wider band than the prior window, so the modelled range runs roughly 754.39 to 770.81. In the prior read the 760/765 walls straddled spot; now the market has already lost the near wall, which under negative gamma is where dealer hedging tends to extend a move rather than dampen it. The gamma playbook still reads range-break-watch with patient conviction, and the prior session was a trend-day-down auction with VWAP 764.84 sitting above spot. This is a structure that has taken one step down and is now leaning on the next shelf: while VIX 15.7 stays calm it can stabilise, but the loss of the 765 wall in short gamma tilts the balance lower. Watch a sustained daily close below 760.00 as the level that would confirm downside continuation toward the lower strikes, whereas a clean reclaim above 765.51 back through the flip would relieve the corridor to the upside.
items.title: SPY spot near 762.6 has slipped below the 765 negative-gamma put wall and under the 765.51 flip, a step down from the prior window when the walls straddled spot

items.method: Cross-read the real-assets per-vehicle scores and the 63-day driver block (crypto and industrial/energy equity proxies versus gold, broad commodities and the gold/silver ratio), track how each vehicle's score changed from the prior window, and set that against the equity sector rotation and the benchmark regime, to judge whether the real-asset bid is broadening or narrowing and whether it agrees with where equity leadership is rotating.
items.note: What is new is that the real-asset bid strengthened across the board rather than narrowing: crypto leadership rose (ETH-USD 74.2/100 and BTC-USD 71.9, both uptrends) and, unlike the prior window, monetary gold GLD ticked up to 48.4 from the low-46 area while broad commodities DBC 62.6 and PDBC 62.6 and industrial copper CPER 59.5 held firm; silver SLV 22.4 stays weak, IBIT 50.1 and oil USO 48.4 are mixed, 14 vehicles scored on a swing horizon. The 63-day driver block still reads risk-on and cyclical — the bitcoin proxy +22.38, energy-equity +7.37 and industrial-equity +5.55 against a gold proxy of only -0.51 and a broad-commodity proxy +0.74 — with the gold-versus-silver ratio proxy +10.89, meaning gold is outpacing silver. Yet equity sector rotation reads the other way defensively: into XLU (Improving, accel +4.53), out of XLF (Weakening, accel +0.46), with XLV (healthcare) Leading. So the real-asset complex is broadening risk-on through crypto, cyclicals and now a firmer gold while equity leadership leans defensive; the widening tension is whether real-asset strength pulls equity leadership back toward risk or converges down to the cautious equity read. VIX 15.7 is calm but the benchmark has slipped to about 2% under its high, so watch a daily close below 760.00 on SPY as the level that would tip the divergence toward the defensive equity side resolving down.
items.title: Real-asset leadership broadened up this window — ETH-USD 74.2 and BTC-USD 71.9 plus gold GLD lifting to 48.4 — while equity sector rotation stayed defensive into XLU with XLV leading
